subject: Math
text_verbatim: Chapter 1 Numberland Adventures: Up to 999 Leap and Learn The number in the brackets is the rounded-off number. Rounding off means a number is made simple but close to the actual number. Let me show you how we can round off a number to the nearest ten. We will use a number line to learn to round off. 1. Basket of oranges = 92 92 is between 90 and 100. [number line 90 to 100, 92 marked] When we round off a number to its nearest ten, we look at the ones digit. If the ones digit is less than five, we have to round down. If the ones digit is five or more, we have to round up. [number line 90-100 with 'round down' arrow pointing left from 95 to 90, and 'round up' arrow pointing right from 95 to 100] The ones digit in 92 is 2. 2 is less than five, so we round down. [number line 90-100 with green arrow from 92 pointing left to 90] 15
